The two classification attacks both fail in the right direction: OBL-G31-NAMING-CANDIDATE carries leftoverDesign false in specifiedNotLeftover, scoped strictly to the naming claim, while OBL-NT-11-EXECUTION carries leftoverDesign true and stands as the sole leftover because no live DR-G* owns that remainder — so the naming close is not permitted to leak into the execution close. G31 is verifiably not live: the register shows zero DR-G31 occurrences and the DR-G row count is still 30, and required-now stays 26 on both the artifact and the register. The strongest claim in the file is the one I recomputed rather than read — authoredFixtureAudit asserts 11 classes, 11 primaries, 17 files present and 0 sha256 mismatches, and walking the pinned corpus and hashing every fixture on disk reproduces all four figures exactly, with 11 primaries plus 6 also-bytes making the 17 and zero files missing. The G31 specification is pinned by bytes without borrowing a verdict, its basedOn entry carrying only path, sha256 and role and stating expressly that no verdict is pinned. The live DR-104 token is DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED, matching the artifact, which correctly inverts the usual framing to say leftover-design/OPEN against this row would be a finding rather than the token. Every cited digest matches with zero mismatches, recordedInputs.HEAD equals the top-level head and live HEAD, no twelfth class is admitted, no G15 ride is forced, no D-* number is assigned, and the subject did not move.
